$comment: Machine-readable companion to STORY.md. Designed to be dropped straight into a visual story tool. Every fact here is recomputed from the shipped package or sourced to a named artifact.
subject: 13-database BIRD-style text-to-SQL package

phases.label: Intake
phases.one_liner: Five months of qualification, contracting and onboarding before a single table existed.

phases.label: Apprentice deliveries
phases.one_liner: Small deliveries that turned out to be the specification.

phases.label: Pathfinders
phases.one_liner: db-6 and db-9 invent the format the other eleven inherit.

phases.label: Industrialization
phases.one_liner: Thirteen databases built in a single day of batch execution.

phases.label: Feedback loop
phases.one_liner: Client accepts the databases, rejects the descriptions. The complaint gets measured.

events.title: First spec arrives
events.detail: [AfterQuery] Code Eval Requirements — coding-agent evaluation rubric: 5 prompt gates, 9 scored dimensions, 16 error codes.

events.title: NDA + Data Submission Agreement executed
events.detail: Two agreements, signed together. The pairing signals a program where the expert submits data rather than receiving it.

events.title: Counterparty diligence
events.detail: Crunchbase company profile and funding history pulled on the buyer.

events.title: Financial and privacy terms reviewed
events.detail: Financial details and privacy documents collected.

events.title: Project Excel onboarding
events.detail: Eight steps: Slack, platform login, sign legal, Stripe as Individual, training, meet your administrator. Rate not stated.
events.artifact: AfterQuery Experts Project Excel Onboarding Document.pdf

events.title: Project Green onboarding

events.artifact: AfterQuery Experts Project Green Onboarding Document.pdf

events.detail: 8 files, 307 KB: README + docker-compose + database/{schema,data,full_dump}.sql + documentation/{SCHEMA,DATA_DICTIONARY}.md. This shape becomes the house format.

events.title: AFTERQUERY bundle
events.detail: Same skeleton at 8 MB, with DATABASE_README.md.

events.title: db-9 pathfinder created
events.detail: Shipping Intelligence, modeled on Pirate Ship. deliverable.json created_date 2026-02-04; first validation report stamped 20260204-2021.

events.title: db-6 weather pipeline built
events.detail: 34 tables merged from four separate schema files — the most complex database in the package.

events.title: QC catches duplicate queries
events.detail: qc_additional_checks.json @ 20260208-2110: duplicates passed 15, failed 15 — 'Query 16 appears to be duplicate' through Query 30. db-9 is rewritten. The fix never propagates to the other databases.

events.title: The annotation schema is inherited
events.detail: SQL Queries_AfterQuery.docx documents 30 queries as Description/Purpose → SQL → Expected Output. The shipped queries.json uses description / sql / expected_output.

events.title: Working tree consolidated
events.detail: 16 candidates present: db-1 through db-16. db-1, db-4, db-5 will not ship.

events.title: Statement of Work
events.detail: BIRD-SQL / LiveSQLBench program. Full-Service $5,500/db vs Introductory $2,000/db. Initial engagement 11 databases, $60,500, 6–8 weeks, 50/25/25 payment.

events.title: Agreements re-executed; db-2 schema authored
events.detail: NDA and DSA re-executed the same week the SOW is dated.

events.title: Batch extraction
events.detail: Eleven queries.json files extracted in one run, stamped 20260216-2320.

events.title: Two reruns
events.detail: db-6 re-extracted at 20260217-0009 and db-16 at 20260217-0146 — the two most complex databases. db-3 schema authored.

events.title: Industrialization day
events.detail: 06:54 nine schemas · 07:03 db-6 consolidated to 34 tables · 08:28 first queries.json · 17:17 all queries.md · 17:39 all documentation · 17:49 root README · 19:19–19:20 all thirteen ~1 GiB datasets.

events.title: Package shipped
events.detail: client-db.zip — 2,424,282,003 bytes, 97 files, 21 GB extracted.

events.title: SOW revision
events.detail: Second version of the statement of work.

events.title: Meeting 1 — the client's verdict
events.detail: 'Databases look good, only comment: the descriptions are AI-generated.' To-do: make descriptions 100% human-made; express query intent rather than summarize the SQL; longer and more deeply contextualized. Some JSONs do not match their .md. Client to send an ingest file format. Standing concern: complexity and quality must not diminish as the engagement scales.

events.title: Meeting 2 — convert the complaint into a spec
events.detail: Prep sheet: what defines a 5/5 description vs a 1/5? Is the concern SQL correctness, natural-language quality, or both? What does 'AI-generated' specifically mean? Benchmarking against BIRD or Spider? Who signs off? Target execution accuracy or F1? Close by locking a written rubric.

events.title: The complaint, measured
events.detail: Mean description 193 chars. 0 of 390 descriptions use the words intent or purpose. db-2 diverges from its markdown on queries 17 and 20-30. 1,053 near-duplicate SQL pairs found independently — the objective form of the same complaint.

events.title: The regression located
events.detail: Use Case / Business Value / Purpose blocks exist for 11 of 13 databases in the working tree db-N.md files and never shipped. The Feb 18 industrialization optimized for uniformity and regressed the deliverable's richest field. Remediation is recovery plus editing, not authoring from scratch.

known_gaps.title: Promised notebook does not ship
known_gaps.detail: Root README promises 'a notebook for ingest, validation, and environment setup'. find client/ -name '*.ipynb' returns 0. The notebooks exist in the working tree for db-6..db-16 only.

known_gaps.title: 1,053 near-duplicate query pairs
known_gaps.detail: At >=0.99 normalized similarity, in 8 of 13 databases. db-6, db-7, db-8, db-9 and db-15 are clean. Caught in db-9 on 2026-02-08 and fixed there only.

known_gaps.title: complexity field carries no signal
known_gaps.detail: All 390 queries tagged 'moderate'. Cannot support the curriculum sampling the README suggests.

known_gaps.title: Audits ran against seed data
known_gaps.detail: db9_dq_audit reports 80 rows across 14 tables; the shipped dataset is 4.79 GB. All perf audits report cache_hit_ratio 100.0 and every query returns row_count 0.

known_gaps.title: Pipelines configured, never executed
known_gaps.detail: pipeline_metadata.json: every pipeline status 'Configured', execution_count 0, empty execution_logs. Shipped bulk data is synthetic.

known_gaps.title: Template leakage
known_gaps.detail: db-9/deliverable.openapi.yaml still carries db-1 examples: database_name db-1, database_type Chat/Messaging System, total_tables 11.

known_gaps.title: Self-contradicting validation report
known_gaps.detail: db-9 final_comprehensive_validation_report.json records Pass: 1 while logging 'relation "packages" does not exist' and an empty phase-3 block stamped database db-6.

known_gaps.title: Descriptions read as AI-generated
known_gaps.detail: Client's only stated objection. Mean 193 chars, 0/390 naming user intent. Corroborated by 1,053 near-duplicate SQL pairs. Remediation plan in REMEDIATION.md.

known_gaps.title: db-2 queries.json diverges from queries.md
known_gaps.detail: Queries 17 and 20-30: descriptions in the JSON do not appear in the markdown. db-6 and db-11 are 29/30; all others 30/30.

known_gaps.title: Four-lens intent documentation never shipped
known_gaps.detail: db-N.md files for db-6..db-16 carry 30 Use Case / Business Value / Purpose blocks each. Not included in the client package. db-2 and db-3 have no such file.

open_questions.question: Why were db-1, db-4 and db-5 cut?
open_questions.evidence: No file states a reason. All three pass their audits. All three are exports of live third-party production systems. None were migrated to the purpose-built format.
open_questions.inference: Provenance risk — db-1/docs/manual-review-checklist.md contains an unticked Provenance Check requiring the source not be publicly available or webcrawlable.

open_questions.question: How did 11 scoped databases become 13 shipped?
open_questions.evidence: SOW dated 2026-02-14 scopes 11 at $5,500/db = $60,500. Thirteen shipped. No change order in the tree.
open_questions.inference: Not determined. At Standard-tier pricing the difference is $11,000.

open_questions.question: Which artifact did the client review when flagging db-2, db-3, db-6, db-7, db-10 as missing intent/purpose fields?
open_questions.evidence: No shipped queries.json has an intent or purpose field — the gap is universal, not specific to those five. db-N_deliverable.json drops question and evidence entirely.
open_questions.inference: The complaint likely describes db-N_deliverable.json or an earlier revision. Confirm before remediating.

open_questions.question: How many databases is this engagement actually for, and at what rate?
open_questions.evidence: Four counts appear: 11 (SOW), 13 (shipped), 14 ('this initial 14'), 16 (stated price point). Two rates: $5,500/db in the SOW, $3,500/db in the working record with $3,000-4,000 indicated at scale.
open_questions.inference: Unreconciled. The spread across a 13-16 database batch is roughly $26,000-32,000.

open_questions.question: What is the acceptance rubric?
open_questions.evidence: Meeting 2 prep asks for a written spec, a 5/5 vs 1/5 example, and a target execution accuracy or F1. None appear in any artifact.
open_questions.inference: Acceptance is currently defined by one sentence of client impression. A rewrite without a rubric is a guess with a cost attached.
